records.title: Operational research as a wartime decision-support discipline
records.sourceNativeSummary: Civilian scientists were embedded into anti-submarine and other operational staffs to analyze search patterns, tactics, equipment use and operational statistics. The effective artifact was a decision loop linking field observations, analysis and command changes, not a detached mathematical report.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Tactical improvement depended on intelligence, aircraft/escort availability and command authority; attribution to “operations research” alone would collapse a multi-component campaign into one analytic layer.

sources.supports: Operations Research Group structure and theoretical/statistical operational analysis

records.title: Feedback amplification and servomechanism engineering
records.sourceNativeSummary: Harold Black’s negative-feedback amplifier addressed instability/distortion in cascaded telephone repeaters by sacrificing open-loop gain for a more stable closed-loop response. The same feedback logic later spread into control/servo engineering.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Feedback is not unconditionally stabilizing: loop gain/phase and plant dynamics can create oscillation. Its value is conditional on a modeled/observed regime rather than a universal “more feedback” rule.

sources.supports: 1927 Bell Labs negative-feedback amplifier and repeater stability problem
Black’s invention/testing, carrier-system pressure and later application

records.title: 1919 eclipse expedition as a high-profile general-relativity test
records.sourceNativeSummary: The 1919 total-eclipse observations attempted to discriminate Einstein’s predicted gravitational bending of starlight from alternative expectations, using eclipse conditions to observe stars near the Sun. The result became a public validation event for general relativity.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The eclipse did not validate every consequence of relativity and measurement uncertainty/analysis choices remained historically debated; one celebrated test should not be treated as a universal evaluator.

sources.supports: historical eclipse-test chronology and later reconfirmation

records.title: Lemaître–Hubble expanding-universe evidence/model transition
records.sourceNativeSummary: Lemaître used relativistic cosmology together with observed galaxy distances/redshifts to infer expansion before Hubble’s 1929 distance–velocity relation became the dominant observational representation. Multiple theory and measurement lineages converged on an expanding universe.
records.rivalOrBoundary: The empirical distance–redshift relation did not uniquely determine later Big Bang cosmology, nor did Hubble alone generate the underlying redshift data; hero compression hides Slipher/Lemaître and model ambiguity.

sources.supports: Slipher data, Lemaître 1927 inference and Hubble observational relation

records.title: Electron microscope opening sub-light-microscope observation
records.sourceNativeSummary: Ruska used electron optics to exploit electron wavelengths shorter than visible light, developing the first electron microscope in 1933 and opening a new observation channel for structures beyond optical-microscope resolution.
records.rivalOrBoundary: A new observation channel did not automatically yield interpretable biological/material truth: sample preparation, vacuum, contrast, beam damage and image interpretation remained new constraints.

sources.supports: electron lens and first electron microscope in 1933

records.title: Cyclotron plus neutron/positron/radiation instrumentation expanding particle physics
records.sourceNativeSummary: Accelerators and particle/radiation detectors changed nuclear/particle research from reliance on naturally occurring radiation toward controllable beams and event observations. New particles/reactions became experimentally reachable because the apparatus changed the intervention/observation frontier.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Bigger energy or more counts did not guarantee correct interpretation; detector signatures, backgrounds and theoretical identification remained separate evidence layers.

sources.supports: cyclotron and artificial high-energy particle acceleration

records.title: All-metal stressed-skin transport aircraft and DC-3 operational diffusion
records.sourceNativeSummary: All-metal cantilever/stressed-skin aircraft combined aerodynamics, structural design, reliable engines and airline operations. The DC-3’s 1935 design became unusually successful because it could carry passengers reliably/economically within a growing route and airport system.
records.rivalOrBoundary: Aircraft performance alone did not produce an airline network; route rights, airports, maintenance, crew, weather/navigation and demand were complements. Military production volumes also should not be read as civilian economic optimum.

sources.supports: 1935 DC-3 design, operating economics, reliability and production
all-metal aircraft transition and DC-series system lineage
